- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-77.5+ peaks, model often overshoots to 78+).
- Underestimate downward corrections when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.10 to -0.30) — model tends to ignore short-term mean reversion.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean to account for bearish momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment drops sharply but is followed by a 2–3 day recovery, model should not reverse direction immediately.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >10% above model, check if sentiment was positive in last 5 days — if yes, model may be underestimating bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.00–0.10) and price is rising, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative and price is near recent high, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid “double dip” bias.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 1–2% below model, consider sentiment as “neutral” — model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 10 days.
